speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a chronic wound on your right lower leg; can you tell me how long it has been present and what it looks like? To better understand the severity, please describe any pain, drainage, or changes in color you have noticed. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, REQUEST TEST: Basic Metabolic Panel.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: WBC - Within normal limits, Hemoglobin - Within normal limits, Platelets - Within normal limits; Basic Metabolic Panel - NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Large wound on the right lower leg. I also have Chronic leg swelling, Family history of similar leg problems. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: PIELONEPHRITIS is incorrect for a lower leg wound; that affects the kidneys. Please clarify: is the swelling constant or does it improve with elevation, and do you have any redness, warmth, or foul drainage from the wound? REQUEST TEST: C-Reactive Protein, REQUEST TEST: Venous_Doppler_Ultrasound.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: C-Reactive Protein: NORMAL READINGS; Venous_Doppler_Ultrasound: Evidence of venous reflux and obstruction in superficial and deep venous systems of the right leg

speaker: Doctor
text: The Doppler ultrasound confirms venous reflux and obstruction, which explains the swelling and likely the chronic wound; the normal C-Reactive Protein suggests this is not an active acute bacterial infection. Given your family history of similar leg problems, do you notice the swelling gets worse at the end of the day and improves after sleeping or elevating your leg? REQUEST IMAGES: Right_Leg_Vein_Duplex

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Deep vein thrombosis in the right leg 5 years prior. No other significant medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works as an accountant.

speaker: Doctor
text: That history of deep vein thrombosis five years ago strongly supports a diagnosis of post-thrombotic syndrome; have you experienced recurrent swelling or skin discoloration like brownish pigmentation or ulceration on that leg? REQUEST IMAGES: Right_Leg_Vein_Duplex.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, recent injuries, heart disease, or diabetes.

speaker: Doctor
text: The denial of fever, heart disease, and diabetes further supports a non-infectious, vascular etiology. Given your history of DVT, current venous reflux, and family history, have you noticed any specific skin changes like brownish discoloration, hardening of the skin (lipodermatosclerosis), or hair loss on that leg? DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-thrombotic Syndrome
